questions.question: Which mechanism allows a transformer to model relationships between all tokens in a sequence?
questions.explanation: Self-attention lets every token attend to every other token, producing contextual representations — the defining feature of the architecture.

questions.question: Why do transformers need positional encodings?
options: The architecture has no recurrence, so order must be injected
questions.explanation: With no recurrence or convolution, the model has no inherent notion of token order — positional encodings add that information to the embeddings.

questions.question: What advantage does multi-head attention provide over a single attention function?
options: It removes the need for embeddings
It attends to different representation subspaces in parallel
questions.explanation: Multiple heads let the model jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.

questions.question: Which claim best explains why transformers train faster than RNNs?
options: Their computation over a sequence is parallelisable
questions.explanation: RNNs process tokens sequentially; transformers process the whole sequence at once, so training parallelises across the sequence dimension.

questions.question: You need contextual token representations for a long document. Based on this page, the most suitable core mechanism is:
questions.explanation: Self-attention handles long-range dependencies directly, which is why it is preferred for long-context representation tasks.
